pk.context: 1300 mg oral, single dose, healthy adults

tell: A lysine-derived antifibrinolytic that is not recommended alongside all-trans retinoic acid, given its thrombotic risk.

clues.text: Absolute bioavailability is approximately 45%, and it may be taken with or without food. It is only 3% bound to plasma proteins, and more than 95% is excreted unchanged in urine.
A synthetic crystalline powder, freely soluble in water, with a molecular weight of 157.2.
Approved under an NDA as 650 mg tablets, taken as 1300 mg three times daily.
No boxed warning. Contraindicated with combined hormonal contraception, active thromboembolic disease and hypersensitivity to it; headache and back pain are common.
Cyclic heavy menstrual bleeding in females of reproductive potential.
Occupies the lysine binding sites of plasmin and plasminogen, preventing plasmin from binding and dissolving fibrin, which preserves the fibrin matrix.
The generic name begins with T and has two words and fourteen letters.
